title: plugin-security: `claimSeedOwnership` re-owns every ownerless row to the platform admin on each `app:seeded`, not only seed rows, so a record an app keeps unowned on purpose leaves its audience after any restart
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named producer and a reproduction; a `finding`, class a (runtime behaviour that contradicts the producer's own stated contract), measured at a public door.
`reach:` HotCRM on `@objectstack/*` 18.0.0-next.1 (branch of objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2116, base `main` `421bd1d8`), local database, the public support form `/_console/f/support`. Measured by the `repo:hotcrm` seat's dev while working objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2060 item 4 (report comment `6183758498`).
Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`session_01P8mZuzuyZAHSrgQKmv6ASv`). The seat re-read the producer on objectstack `origin/main` `16abea884`. ⛔ Not a claim.
Reader: objectstack triage, then the lane that owns `packages/plugins/plugin-security`.
Dedupe (MCP `search_issues`, objectstack, open + closed): "claim seed ownership re-owns unowned rows owner_id null on every restart app:seeded" → 1 hit, #14157 (closed: `maybeSeedDevAdmin` gating on any `sys_user` row), a different defect.

## Seen

1. With the Service Agent position empty, an anonymous submission of the support form (`POST /api/v1/forms/support/submit` → 201) creates a `crm_case` with `owner_id = null`. That is intended: HotCRM's criteria rule `case_unassigned_triage_sharing` (`record.owner_id == null && status not resolved/closed` → `edit` for position `service_agent`) is the triage queue for exactly these rows.
2. Once the pool is staffed and the rule evaluated, `service.agent` reads the case (CASE-00045: `GET` 200, `owner_id` null).
3. After a plain `objectstack start` restart, the same case is owned by the platform admin `admin@objectos.ai`, and the agent's `GET` answers 404. CASE-00040, -42 and -43 went the same way on a dev watch auto-restart: `updated_at` = the boot instant, `updated_by` null.

So every restart empties the app's "Unassigned — Triage" queue and hands the backlog to an identity that holds no app capability. No seed row is involved: these cases were created at runtime by a public form.

## Producer

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts`:
- `UNOWNED_PREDICATES` (L234-237) is `[{ owner_id: null }, { owner_id: SystemUserId.SYSTEM }]`, applied by `claimSeedOwnership` to every object that declares `owner_id` (filters (a)–(d) in its docblock: not `managedBy`, not `sys_*`, not `external`). Nothing narrows it to rows a seed wrote.
- `security-plugin.ts` L1565-1566 subscribes `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` to `app:seeded`, which fires on every boot (the header, L14-16: "again whenever a seed settles (`app:seeded`) on every boot — the first one and every later one").
- In the installed 18.0.0-next.1 `dist/index.js` the same code sits around L8025-8030 and L9903-9917.

The header's contract (L47-49) is "Idempotent: only NULL / `usr_system`-owned rows are touched, so once a real admin owns them a re-run is a no-op." That holds for seed rows. It does not hold for a row an app leaves unowned by design: `owner_id = null` is a legitimate runtime state (a queue, a web-to-X intake, a pooled record), and the claim cannot tell it apart from an orphaned seed row.

## Expected

The claim re-owns rows the seed wrote, and leaves alone rows created at runtime with no owner. Ways the platform could tell them apart are for the owning lane to choose; for example, the seeder records which ids it wrote and the claim walks only those, or an object can opt out.

## Acceptance

- On an app whose seed has settled once, a `crm_case`-like row created at runtime with `owner_id = null` keeps `owner_id = null` across a restart; a criteria share keyed on `owner_id == null` still reaches its recipients afterwards.
- A seeded row with no `owner_id` is still handed to the first platform admin, on first boot and on an over-budget background settle (the cases the header's "NOT a single pass" section exists for).
